description: Original ST1221 FFT, strong-peak and geometry routines are retained in analysis_core.py; fixed search now exposes its unpruned hypothesis pool. scale_fitting.py adds bounded local scale fitting and scale costs. peak_evidence.py separately audits weak/missing predictions. phase_comparison.py retains conservative shared-strong-evidence ambiguity. adaptive_refinement.py compares alternatives on the same child pixels. Independent and parent-related direct-diffraction candidates share score_prediction_nodes and prediction-site evidence; spot_intensity.py supplies phase-independent integrated signal weights. brightness_grouping.py adds a bounded soft preference for phase brightness groups after geometric assignment. FFT power is now integrated for the same soft grouping preference, and measured profile IDs rank integrated brightness.
limits: Finite HCP/BCC/FCC/ORT/OMEGA template library and constrained beta/omega candidates; untested structures and orientations can affect the result.
Compatibility scores are not phase probabilities.
Fourier support is not phase fraction.
Automatic searches are bounded and not guaranteed global optima.
Two-scale HCP fits have more flexibility. The scale-magnitude penalty is not a statistical correction for the number of fitting parameters.
A zone containing no c-sensitive reflections cannot determine HCP c.
The shared-evidence ambiguity guard is conservative and heuristic; it is not calibrated statistical model selection.
Scale penalty is an adjustable quadratic preference relative to reference dimensions, not a measured strain limit; calibration offsets can affect ranking.
Weak/missing prediction checks and rotated controls are heuristic, not statistical significance or a physical contrast-transfer/intensity model.
Passing-parent child checks use a limited candidate search and heuristic margin; smaller windows may lose information, and hidden finer structures can remain undetected.

Direct diffraction is an experimental spot-pattern mode, not ring indexing. Beam centre, reciprocal calibration, masks and detection thresholds need inspection. Opposite-pair centre estimation can select a lattice-equivalent inversion centre; local contrast and estimated widths are heuristic.

Parent-linked beta/omega uses relative geometry and an ideal orientation relationship. Shared reflections are ambiguous; the common positional and prediction-evidence scores are heuristic. It does not infer absolute cell size, phase fraction, incomplete-collapse structure or dynamical diffraction. Nominal omega absence coincidences are geometric diagnostics, not explained intensities or extra allowed-reflection evidence.

extensions.beta_omega.py: related-patterns-common-score-v6: parent/variant geometry generation and assignment reporting; all union subsets use analysis_core.score_prediction_nodes and peak_evidence. No separate geometry/compactness rank or forced near-tied selection. Four ideal variants remain constrained by one parent. Linked assignments use the shared soft positional kernel and export per-profile quality. The common distance scale is used without an additional linked-only cap. All active parent-linked omega variants share one 0.025 phase-family addition cost; beta-only costs zero. Per-variant exclusive/nonparallel support and joint missing-site evidence remain mandatory. Independent orientations keep their per-addition cost.
extensions.scale_fitting.py: Automatic uniform HCP/BCC or independent HCP basal/c reciprocal scales. Same bounded zones, wider reflection band, scale bounds 0.85–1.15. Each fitted hypothesis receives an optional mean squared scale-deviation penalty before ranking and zone selection. Default strength 0.10 per 5% adjustment, zero disables; fitted positions are unchanged by the ranking cost. Distinct zone hypotheses can be retained for the same observed profile set.
extensions.phase_comparison.py: shared-evidence-v1: reports matched/unsupported prediction counts and adds an exact-shared-profile ambiguity guard. Operates on the rank score supplied by fitting; does not adjust positional scores, simulate intensities, assume allowed reflections must be present, or automatically prefer the sparser model.
extensions.peak_evidence.py: local-maxima-v6: phase-independent weak-maxima pool; one-to-one matching with the common soft positional kernel, local-background contrast and rotated controls. Independent weak bonus (0–0.5) and missing penalty (0–2). Every prediction assigned to a detected profile incurs zero missing-site cost, including displaced matches and cached v5 records; positional agreement charges the displacement. Weak support relieves at most half a missing-site cost. Unsupported sites retain full missing fraction, unchecked sites are excluded, and radial attenuation applies to deficits. Physical footprints for border, mask and neighbour assessment are separate from the distortion-aware positional scale. Raw detections and separate-pattern screens are unchanged.
extensions.adaptive_refinement.py: passing-children-v2: optional four-child trial after a parent passes. Keep children for separate strong patterns, a resolved alternative beating the parent family on the same child by 0.08 (or passing when that family fails), or mixed passing and unresolved/insufficient/ambiguous assignments. Retain a parent when all children simply lose evidence or the trial is interrupted. Rescoring preserves boundaries and original refinement decisions.
extensions.diffraction.py: direct-spots-v1: reciprocal-calibrated DM4 detector analysis without an FFT. Opposite-spot midpoint centre estimate near the detector midpoint, editable centre/calibration, Gaussian local-contrast spot detector with centroid positions, signed observations grouped as opposite profiles, rectangular and central exclusions. Reuses bounded HCP/BCC comparison and geometry checks in the 3–10 nm^-1 band. Hidden/outside positions are unchecked in prediction-site audits.
extensions.double_diffraction.py: observed-two-step-v1 / weighted-dd-v1: observed allowed source beams, both measured and fitted sums required, bounded additional-profile quality score weighted by measured fitting importance and supported observed signs. DD weight 0–1 defaults to zero. Each target counts once; multiplicity gives no bonus, allowed targets are excluded. Single-scattering acceptance and missing costs remain unchanged. Every independent candidate and explicit ordinary/related union is evaluated before ranking; alternative hypotheses never exchange beams. Cached FFT/grid reweighting reuses saved measurements. This is heuristic geometric evidence, not a dynamical intensity model.
extensions.diffraction_fitting.py: Unified direct-diffraction phase-selection pipeline. Relative/Unknown images use normalized independent searches and the same beta hypotheses whether omega is selected or disabled. Related candidates and ordinary primary+secondary unions share positional, weak/missing and additional-pattern costs. All scored ordinary unions export explicit selection and component records, including same-phase orientations, FFT and brightness disabled; a union must pass and improve on the primary to be selected. Actual passing rival scores are exposed; common near-tie margin 0.08. Finite searches are not guaranteed global optima. DD weighting also allows independently supported ordinary pairs to compete without requiring brightness evidence; same-phase pairs are eligible. Calibrated BCC parents recover canonical rotation and handedness jointly from indexed fitted positions; the legacy template mirror flag is not transferred directly.
extensions.spot_intensity.py: aperture-photometry-v2: native detector-pixel and native linear FFT-power aperture integrals above a robust local plane. Exact discrete aperture fractions, overlap partitioning and incomplete/background checks; opposite observations/conjugates averaged once. FFT apertures use equivalent detected-component radius plus one window-response FWHM (minimum 2 bins), retain neighbouring components as exclusions even when selection controls remove them, and do not interpret Fourier maxima as camera clipping. FFT retains original enrichment weights. Both spectrum types assign profile IDs by descending integrated signal before fitting, without changing fitting input order; automatic-strength trials renumber copies of their selected subsets.
extensions.brightness_grouping.py: soft-brightness-v3: reliable positive integrated native detector signal or FFT power; detector clipping and incomplete/overlapping apertures are excluded. Robust log-signal fit compares one level against nonnegative additive levels per phase with a common fitted radial trend; omega variants share one level. Shared observations count once. Requires at least six reliable matched profiles and full-rank membership groups with at least two nonparallel profiles each. Loss scale log(2), log signal clipped to median ± log(32), extra-level cost 0.5 × (phase count − 1) × log(N). Nonnegative gain becomes matched-reliable fraction × (1 − exp(−2 × gain/N)), bounded by one. Adjustable 0–0.5 rank bonus, default 0.10; zero disables the preference. Geometry, missing-site and independent-pattern screens cannot be rescued by brightness. Single phases remain neutral; no hard beta-brighter prior or intensity/phase-fraction simulation. Ordinary supported phase pairs and constrained parent/variant subsets compete in the common pipeline. Direct rescoring reconsiders candidates from stored measurements; FFT/grid rescoring uses stored independent candidates, measured integrals and weak-evidence context to recompute supported combinations without recalculating the FFT. Positional quality weights the robust residuals and the matched-reliable support fraction, so broad associations cannot collect full brightness credit.
extensions.analysis_core.py: soft-cauchy-v1 positional matching: q(d) = max(0, [1/(1+(d/w)^2) − 1/17] / [16/17]); search reach 4w, continuous loss with offset, exact one-to-one assignment. Angular chance support integrates the same kernel analytically, conditional on measured radii, to penalize dense predictions consistently. All crystal phases, independent combinations and linked variants share this rule. Width is an evidence scale, not a hard acceptance radius or a fitted distortion correction. width-plus-relative-distortion-v1: distance scale = hypot(estimated peak width, 0.04 times median measured reciprocal radius), fixed across all direct-diffraction candidates in a spectrum. Both terms follow coordinate rescaling. FFT retains its existing window-response width with a 0.10 floor. This is a ranking allowance, not a fitted distortion correction; physical visibility/assessability footprints remain separate.

fft_processing.options: Hann or rectangular crop; optional mean removal before windowing. Defaults retain the original transform. Approximate power peak widths are 1.44 or 0.886 FFT bins; detection, fitting and weak-peak tolerances use the selected window.
